samples.summary: Step 9 of the originating task (docs) is still unmet: no design doc records the new /api/v1 comments surface, and the capability audit still says it does not exist
samples.evidence: The originating plan `docs/tasks/active/20260904-class-b-backend-endpoints-todo.md` step 9 requires updating `docs/design/agentic-office-workflow.md` (class-B status note), `docs/design/cli.md`, `docs/design/rest-api.md` and `packages/backend/README.md`. In the working tree: `rest-api.md` §5 enumerates endpoint families 5.1–5.9 with no comments section (grep for 'comments' in that file returns nothing); `docs/design/cli.md` has no mention of the new `comments` CLI namespace even though `packages/cli/src/commands/comments.ts` exists; `packages/backend/README.md` has no mention; and `docs/design/agentic-office-workflow.md:213` still asserts 'No comment controller under `/api/v1`; comments live in the Yorkie CRDT and never pass through the backend', which this PR makes false. The canonical docs now describe a system that no longer matches the code. This delta is test-only, so this is a PR-level gap that the added doc/pdf coverage does not change; cost is documentation drift, not broken behavior.

samples.summary: The new flat-root fixture hand-rolls the thread/comment shape instead of reusing the canonical builders, and stores number timestamps where the real CRDT stores BigInt
samples.evidence: `flatRoot()` builds `{ comments: { t1: { id, anchor, comments: [{ id, author, body, createdAt: 5 }], resolved, createdAt: 5 } } }` by hand, while `packages/backend/src/yorkie/comment-ops.ts` exports `buildThread`/`buildReply` (which route through `createThread`/`addReply` in @wafflebase/sheets) as the single source of that shape, and `toYorkieMs` (comment-ops.ts:59) stores every timestamp as a BigInt — the boundary the originating task step 2 explicitly calls out. The docs anchor is likewise abbreviated to `{ kind: 'docs-range', blockId: 'b1' }`, omitting the `posRange`/`quotedText` the real `docs-range` anchor carries (packages/frontend/src/types/comments.ts). The fixture therefore encodes a shape the product never writes, so the flat-root branch is proven only against a schema that can drift from the canonical one; a `buildThread`-seeded fixture would stay tied to it.

samples.summary: The new describe.each block restates the sheet authorship suite's cases rather than parameterizing the existing one over all three types
samples.evidence: 'ApiV1CommentsController edit / delete authorship' (line 453) and the new 'edit / delete authorship on a %s' block (line 541) assert the same six behaviours (author-only edit, empty body, non-author delete, own reply delete, opening-comment-deletes-thread, non-opener thread delete) with duplicated PEER constants and near-identical bodies. A single `describe.each` over sheet/doc/pdf with a per-type seeding helper would keep the two from diverging when the lifecycle rule changes. Taste-level; the coverage itself is a genuine addition.
